applicableAreas: site boundaries where overhead electric lines are present
findings.comment: Overhead electric (OHE) lines are present on western and southern property boundaries, serving as customer facilities on adjacent properties. Horizontal sky-to-ground clearances from the outermost overhead conductor to buildings, transformers, pull boxes, and meters are not dimensioned on the electrical design plan or site plan sheets. Clearances cannot be verified without explicit horizontal measurements from the outside conductor to each customer facility edge.

applicableAreas: site boundaries and building locations where overhead distribution conductors are present
findings.comment: Overhead electric lines are present on property boundaries. The required 15-foot radial clearance zones from the outside conductor to customer facilities (buildings, transformers, pull boxes) are not graphically delineated or annotated on the plans. The simultaneous compliance requirement with both 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances cannot be verified from the submitted documents.

applicableAreas: transformer pad locations and meter vault locations
findings.comment: Electrical meters are shown attached to all eight buildings and four transformer pads are located throughout the site (Sheet 21). The required 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance from these customer service entrance facilities to AE poles and overhead lines (other than the service drop) is not dimensioned on the electrical design plan. Compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: overhead service-drop routing across site areas
findings.comment: The preliminary electrical design shows overhead electric lines on property boundaries. Service-drop vertical clearances over truck traffic areas (construction access drives, parking areas, loading zones) are not identified or dimensioned on the utility plan. The applicable clearance (18 feet for truck-accessible areas, 16 feet for residential-only areas) cannot be verified from submitted plans.

applicableAreas: multiple utility crossing locations throughout site
findings.comment: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) depicts multiple perpendicular crossings of underground electric lines (red dashed) with water (blue), wastewater (purple), and storm drain (green) lines throughout the site. The required 12-inch minimum clearance—both horizontally and vertically—is not specified at any crossing point. Contractor utility notes (Block 6) require verification of conflicts but do not mandate the specific 12-inch separation. Crossing details with labeled clearance dimensions must be provided or measurements obtained.

applicableAreas: all utility crossings over or under water, wastewater, and storm drain mains
findings.comment: The utility tap plan shows multiple proposed utilities crossing existing and proposed water, wastewater, and storm drain lines (Sheet 19). The crossing method—whether trenchless bore or open-cut—is not identified on any plan sheet or detail. Without crossing method identification, the applicable separation standard cannot be determined: trenchless requires 2× excavation diameter or 36 inches (whichever is greater); open-cut requires 12 inches (water main above) or 18 inches (water main below). Crossing details must specify method and provide labeled separation dimensions.

applicableAreas: utility crossings under roads, structures, and barriers
findings.comment: The utility tap public plan and profile (Sheet 20) show water line installation in the public right-of-way but do not include encasement specifications for the bore section. No crossing detail sheets provide material type, dimensions, or longitudinal extent of any encasement sleeves or concrete casing. Encasement specifications per UCM 2.9.1.D and City of Austin standard details must be added to the utility crossing detail sheets.

applicableAreas: storm drain manhole locations relative to overhead electric poles
findings.comment: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows three storm drain (SD) manholes: one central (between Buildings 3 and 4), one east-central (north of Building 7), and one south of Building 4 near the southern property line. The southern SD manhole is positioned near the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern boundary. No horizontal clearance dimensions between any manhole and any Austin Energy overhead pole are provided on the plan. The required 5-foot horizontal separation cannot be verified from available documents.

Sheet 3, Block 20 references a transmission easement with specific requirements including maintenance of a 25-foot-wide access corridor with 16-foot minimum vertical clearance. However, the transmission easement boundary is not delineated on the site plan (Sheet 9), grading plan (Sheet 11), or erosion control plan (Sheet 5). No labeled 25-foot-wide access corridor with 16-foot vertical clearance dimensions is shown on any construction or staging plan sheet. The transmission ROW access requirement cannot be verified from submitted plans.

applicableAreas: SCM staging area on western side of property
findings.comment: The biofiltration-detention pond (Sheet 15) has a water quality volume of 6,388 cubic feet and maximum ponding depth of 3.65 feet, exceeding the 5,000-cubic-foot and 3-foot exemption thresholds. Therefore, a permanent SCM staging area is required and subject to 14-foot minimum vertical clearance from existing and proposed vegetation and all other objects. Sheet 5 (Erosion Control Plan) shows a 'Staging and Storage Area' on the western side of the property adjacent to Building 2, but no 14-foot vertical clearance dimension is labeled. Clearance must be demonstrated with annotation on the plans.

The SCM pond volume (6,388 cubic feet) and ponding depth (3.65 feet) exceed exemption thresholds, triggering the requirement for maintenance access drives with 14-foot minimum vertical clearance from vegetation at maturity and all other objects. No 14-foot vertical clearance dimensions are labeled on any plan sheet (site plan, grading plan, or erosion control plan). All maintenance access drive corridors must be annotated with 14-foot clearance heights, accounting for vegetation at maturity.

applicableAreas: staging and temporary spoils area locations
findings.comment: Sheet 3, Block 20 (Electric Transmission Notes) explicitly prohibits placement of staging and spoils areas within 20 feet of transmission structures and requires that all materials remain outside the transmission easement. However, the transmission easement boundary is not delineated on the site plan or construction drawings, and the staging area shown on Sheet 5 (western side adjacent to Building 2) has no dimensions confirming its distance from the transmission facility. The transmission easement boundary must be graphically shown and the staging area location verified as compliant with the 20-foot buffer requirement.

applicableAreas: site plan and utility plan showing overhead electric lines on property boundaries
findings.comment: Overhead electric lines (OHE) are present on the western and southern property boundaries. Neither the distribution clearance envelope (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial from outside conductor) nor the transmission clearance envelope (requires AE engineering determination) are graphically delineated on any site plan, utility plan, or grading plan sheet. Clearance zones must be shown with dashed boundary lines anchored to the outside conductor, not the pole centerline, clearly identifying the extent of each zone.

applicableAreas: site plan and utility plan sheets
findings.comment: No horizontal dashed height limit lines are shown on the site plan (Sheet 9), utility plan (Sheet 21), or grading plan (Sheet 11) to delineate the overhead electrical utility clearance envelope boundaries. Height limit lines must be added as horizontal dashed annotations on all relevant plan sheets, clearly marking the extent of the overhead conductor clearance zones and preventing structures or equipment from penetrating the protected airspace.

applicableAreas: site areas with sloped and stepped terrain where overhead utilities are present
findings.comment: The site has non-uniform grade conditions with building finished floor elevations ranging from 683 feet to 687.5 feet and topography varying between the two benchmarks (678.52' and 681.08'). Overhead electric lines are present on property boundaries. No sloped or stepped dashed height limit lines are shown on the grading plan (Sheet 11) or utility plan (Sheet 21) to reflect the actual grade changes beneath the overhead conductor spans. Height limit lines must be stepped or sloped to follow the terrain while maintaining the required minimum clearances at all elevations.
